title: Escrow Rate on Entrance Fee Agreement Deposits by Deposit Size
content:
Treasury memorandum on the escrow rate of the deposit under an **Entrance Fee Agreement**, as it applies to the refund on a resident's own cancellation before occupancy.

The deposit is the only money held in escrow, and the escrow interest is figured on the deposit amount at the escrow rate for the term held. The escrow rate is set by the size of the deposit: a deposit of 40000.00 or more earns 2.05 percent a year, a deposit of 20000.00 to 39999.99 earns 1.55 percent a year, and a smaller deposit carries no escrow rate.

The deposit amount is the total of the deposit payments entered on the agreement's ledger; balance payments are never escrowed.

## Rate ladder

| Escrowed deposit (USD) | Escrow rate per year |
|---|---|
| 40000.00 or more | 2.05 percent |
| 20000.00 to 39999.99 | 1.55 percent |
| Below 20000.00 | 0 percent |

## Both sides of each threshold

| Deposit | Rate |
|---|---|
| 40000.00 | 2.05 |
| 39999.99 | 1.55 |
| 20000.00 | 1.55 |
| 19999.99 | 0 |

## Hypothetical deposits

- A deposit of 37765.00 sits in the middle band: 1.55 percent a year.
- A deposit of 41500.00 sits in the top band: 2.05 percent a year.
- A deposit of 16850.00 is below 20000.00: an escrow rate of 0 percent.
